findings.title: footgun: TransactionResult.clampedPayload reads as 'the payload that will be applied', implying it is meaningful only on success and empty otherwise.
findings.detail: On the failure paths at lines 82-87 (source has no state) and 100-105 (source entry invalid), the returned object has success:false but clampedPayload set to the capacity-clamped payload (non-empty), while the other two failures return {}. A caller that applies clampedPayload without checking success would move resources on a failed transaction; the field's population is inconsistent across failure branches.

findings.title: footgun: status is typed 'completed' | 'extinction' and readStateValue/isExtinct suggest any tick where population<=0 ends the run as extinction.
findings.detail: status only becomes 'extinction' (and the loop breaks) when isExtinct && i > 10 (line 93). If population reaches 0 at loop index <= 10 it is snapshotted but the run continues and, if population stays 0, still returns status:'completed'. Early extinction is silently reported as a completed run.

findings.title: footgun: The variable is named blueprintSettings, implying it holds blueprint-level settings.
findings.detail: It is read from cartridge.config?.settings, and the if/else makes config.settings and assets.settings mutually exclusive: when config.settings is present, cartridge.assets?.settings is never walked, so any asset-defined setting levers are silently omitted whenever config settings also exist.

findings.title: footgun: InstantTransferHandler is registered like any typed handler via runtime.registerCommandHandler.
findings.detail: It is force-cast through `as unknown as CommandHandler<RuntimeCommand>` (it only implements CommandHandler<TransferAssetsCommand>), defeating the compiler check, and registerHandler stores handlers in a Map keyed by handler.type, so this registration silently overwrites any previously-registered TRANSFER_ASSETS handler rather than adding to it.

findings.title: footgun: createCycleCostCondition carries a token form `self.state.<resource>.value >= amountRef`, i.e. the has-enough-resource check reads as a plain >= on the raw resource value.
findings.detail: The runtime evaluator (JsonLogicAdapter.evaluate) uses rule.compiled when present and only compiles from tokens as a fallback, so the authoritative predicate is the compiled `>` on `(resource.value + 1)` vs amountRef (a +1 grace unit), not the token's `>=`. The tokens are dead for evaluation and encode a different boundary; editing the visible token `>=` has zero runtime effect.

findings.title: footgun: createCycleCostPowerGateRule's condition token form is `self.state.<resource>.value < amountRef` (gate power when resource is below the cost).
findings.detail: The compiled form actually evaluated is `(resource.value + 1) <= amountRef` (a +1 grace unit and a <= boundary), so the token `<` is dead and disagrees with the runtime boundary; a maintainer reading or editing the tokens sees the wrong predicate.

findings.title: footgun: createCycleRule's is_active gate condition is `{ t: 'ref', v: 'self.state.cycle_active' }`, reading like a boolean check that the cycle is active (cycle_active is a state entry `{value:1|0}`).
findings.detail: The ref omits `.value`, so it compiles to `{var:'self.state.cycle_active'}` which json-logic-js resolves to the whole state-entry OBJECT (not its numeric value). A non-null object is always truthy, so this gate is truthy even when cycle_active.value is 0; every other compiled condition in the subsystem uses the `.value` suffix. The intended gating is effectively inert here (masked only because conditional-activation also zeroes powerSink.throttle, which zeroes the accumulated allocatedDraw*dt_s).

findings.title: footgun: `toRefPath` is a `switch (condition.kind)` that reads as a total mapping from any structured condition to its state var path.
findings.detail: The union has 9 kinds but the switch only handles 4 (`fact_threshold`, `world_state_threshold`, `world_state_boolean`, `user_interaction`); for the other 5 (`entity_tag_present`, `bodies_assigned`, `body_in_pointer`, `carriers_orbiting`, `destructive_assignment_has_all_bodies`) it falls off the end and returns `undefined`. There is no return-type annotation and no exhaustiveness guard, so this is silent. It is currently harmless only because those 5 kinds return fixed tokens in `toCompiledExpression` and never call `toRefPath`.

findings.title: footgun: The `user_interaction` compiled expression selects `==` vs `!=` via `interaction === "self_selected" ? "==" : "!="`, reading as a two-value toggle between the two documented interaction states.
findings.detail: The ternary is not a match on `"self_unselected"` — any interaction value other than the exact string `"self_selected"` yields `!=`. The schema currently constrains it to those two enums, but the lowering silently treats every non-`self_selected` value (including any future or malformed interaction state) as the unselected/`!=` branch rather than erroring.

findings.title: footgun: namespaceBlueprints is named as though it always namespaces blueprint ids under the file's namespace.
findings.detail: Only ids WITHOUT an explicit `id` field are namespaced; any blueprint carrying a bare explicit `id` (e.g. "cannon") is used verbatim and stays unnamespaced, so two files can produce the same global id and collide during registry merge.

findings.title: footgun: validatePayload guards with `typeof this.linker.linkProject === "function"`, implying it links/loads the project to validate against.
findings.detail: linkProject is never called anywhere in validatePayload; validation is done entirely from the passed-in currentModules map. The guard checks a capability the method does not use, so a linker missing every other method still passes.

findings.title: footgun: The strict .cave schema accepts keys `swarm`, `world`, and `understanding` (line 36/35/39), implying these are valid cartridge config sections.
findings.detail: mergeSemanticFragment deep-merges the whole parsed .cave object into runtime.config, but SysConfigSchema has no `swarm` or `understanding` keys; those values are silently carried as inert extra properties on config and never consumed by the runtime.

findings.title: footgun: deepMergeObjects reads as a full recursive merge that combines base and override for the whole config tree.
findings.detail: Arrays never merge — an override array replaces the base array entirely (line 15), so array-valued config sections (conditions/guidances/tutorials/knowledge) from a later .cave file overwrite rather than accumulate across files.

findings.title: footgun: normalizeRef appears to normalize a 'self.'-prefixed ref, sitting alongside the 'global.'->'globals.' rewrite as if it transforms the string.
findings.detail: 'self.'.length is 5, so `self.${ref.slice(5)}` strips 'self.' and re-prepends the identical 'self.' — the branch is a pure no-op returning ref unchanged. The 'globals.' branch on line 31 is likewise a no-op. Only the 'global.'->'globals.' branch (line 30) actually rewrites anything.

findings.title: footgun: The entity facade's get trap intercepts prop === 'assignment' to derive { parentId } from the assignmentMap, reading as a convenience accessor added on top of the entity.
findings.detail: RuntimeEntity is Record<string, unknown>, so an entity may carry its own real 'assignment' field; the Proxy unconditionally shadows it and always returns the synthesized { parentId }, so any genuine entity.assignment data is unreachable through the facade.

findings.title: footgun: registerOperations is invoked from the JsonLogicAdapter constructor (JsonLogicAdapter.ts:16), reading as per-instance operation registration.
findings.detail: A module-level `opsRegistered` flag (ops.ts:7) makes every call after the first a no-op, and json-logic-js.add_operation mutates the shared singleton import — so QUERY/QUERY_COUNT/SLOT/SUM are registered exactly once and leak globally into every json-logic-js consumer in the process, not scoped to any adapter instance.

findings.title: footgun: resolvePulseScale is documented by its name and by PULSE_DIAMETER_MARGIN_PX to size a pulse blob to fit inside the vein width (widthPx - margin), implying the blob renders at roughly the vein's thickness.
findings.detail: The fit-to-width scale is immediately multiplied by an unexplained `* 3` (plus the variance multiplier), so blobs render about 3x the vein width. The margin subtraction is effectively cosmetic; the 'fit the stroke' intent the helper name and margin constant imply does not hold at runtime.

findings.title: footgun: VeinEdgeVisualState.lastIntensity01 (seeded from edge.intensity01 in createEdgeState and reassigned every tick) reads as edge animation state that drives rendering, e.g. a rising/falling-intensity effect.
findings.detail: lastIntensity01 is write-only: it is assigned in veinsEdgeTick.ts:117 and seeded in veinsEdgeState.ts:37 but never read by any non-test code. It influences nothing on screen; intensity01 is dead as far as this render path is concerned.

findings.title: footgun: getShapeTexture is called with color:"#ffffff", suggesting the pulse shape texture is generated white and the vein's actual color is baked into the texture here.
findings.detail: The color argument is a placeholder only; the real pulse color comes later from setTint(variance.tint) in spawnPulse (veinsPulseLifecycle.ts:38). The white here exists solely so the texture is tintable; reading this line as 'pulses are white' is wrong.

findings.title: footgun: The `if (visual.ropeSignature !== lastSignature)` guard presents as a cache that skips the expensive rope re-sync on frames where nothing changed.
findings.detail: resolveCycleProgressVisual builds the signature from a payload that includes timeMs and pulseValue (cycleProgressVisual.ts:42-47), both of which change every animated frame, so the signature almost never matches lastSignature. The guard skips work only when the node is paused/static; in normal play syncCycleProgressRope runs every frame and the cache buys nothing.

findings.title: footgun: countBlobsThatFitSourceGap and resolveBlobSpacing (veinsVisualMath.ts:85) read as the vein pulse-spawning algorithm and are covered by tests, implying they run in production.
findings.detail: Neither has any non-test caller. The live spawn logic in veinsPulseTick.ts computes spacing and gap fitting inline with different code; these exports are an abandoned/parallel implementation that green tests make look load-bearing.

findings.title: footgun: styleImage assigns blend as a plain AvatarImageStyle.blend number, and renderAvatarStack passes literal blend: 1 (glow/eyes) and blend: 0 (silhouette), reading like arbitrary flags.
findings.detail: These integers are Phaser blend-mode enum values: 0 is NORMAL and 1 is ADD (per display/blendModes BLEND_MODE_NORMAL=0 / BLEND_MODE_ADD=1). The glow and eyes are additively blended and the silhouette is normal; the named constants exist but are bypassed with magic numbers.

findings.title: footgun: resolveBlink reads as returning a blink amount (higher = more blinking).
findings.detail: It returns eye OPENNESS: 1 means fully open / not blinking (window > durationMs branch), and it dips toward 0 at the midpoint of the blink window. It is consumed as openness (openness = Math.max(0.04, blink)); the name is inverted relative to the value.

findings.title: footgun: normalizeThickness(shape, thickness) reads as clamping/rounding a stroke width to a valid value for every shape.
findings.detail: For shapes in its ignore-set (crescent, hole, triangle, star5, star6, circle, pixel, triple_circle) it returns 0, discarding the caller's requested thickness entirely; that 0 is then baked into the texture cache key (line 49-55), so different requested thicknesses for those shapes silently share one cached texture, while the draw call falls back to 10 via `thickness || 10`.

findings.title: footgun: resolveGlyphPlacementColor prefers the palette-keyed color when a paletteColorKey is set.
findings.detail: It uses `paletteColor || placement.colorHex`, so a palette entry resolving to an empty string (or any falsy value) is treated as absent and silently falls through to the literal colorHex, even though the palette key is present.

findings.title: footgun: A module named glyphShapeDrawFnsRings exporting drawCircle/drawRing/drawHexRing/drawOctRing/drawSquareRing/drawPixel, implying these ring draw functions are the ring-rendering implementation.
findings.detail: Only the trailing GLYPH_TEXTURE_SIZE constant is imported anywhere; none of the exported draw functions have a consumer. Live ring rendering is done by glyphTextureDrawStroke.ts. The file's name and its exported functions misrepresent what is actually used.

findings.title: footgun: assertAvatarAppearance(appearance) reads as a full validation of the AvatarAppearance record.
findings.detail: It only checks that appearanceKey is a non-empty string and returns; every other field (indices, scales, blink timing) is unvalidated, so a malformed appearance with a set key passes the 'assert' unchecked.

findings.title: footgun: validateScratchSlots reads as a validation that throws or blocks on leaked per-instance scratch objects at destroy time.
findings.detail: On finding leaked slots (backgroundImage/mainImage/particlesManager/rope/graphics still set) it only console.errors and returns; it does not clear or destroy them, so the leak proceeds and the anchors are released anyway.

findings.title: footgun: setScratchAlpha(scratch, alpha) named as if it sets the whole instance's alpha.
findings.detail: It sets alpha on exactly one object, backgroundImage if present otherwise root, leaving the other four anchors (effects/overlay/background container, etc.) untouched; full-instance dimming only happens because a separate 5-anchor setter is paired with it in the tutorial-attention path.

findings.title: footgun: readNonEmptyString(value) reads as returning a trimmed non-empty string.
findings.detail: It tests value.trim() for emptiness but returns the ORIGINAL untrimmed value; a seed like ' abc ' is returned with its whitespace, and only gets trimmed later inside AvatarAppearanceRegistry.resolve.

findings.title: footgun: release(obj) paired with acquire() suggests symmetric in-use accounting.
findings.detail: acquire optionally runs a custom acquireFn (which for pools is activatePooledObject and does NOT call resetFn), so a reused object is reset only on release; the resetFn fallback inside acquire only runs when no acquireFn was supplied, which is never the case for the real container/image/rope/graphics pools.

findings.title: footgun: resolveNervousDeliveredRate(edge, entityById, graph) is named and typed as if it computes a nervous edge's delivered flow rate from the edge, the entity map, and the graph.
findings.detail: All three parameters are prefixed with _ and ignored; the body unconditionally returns 0. Every nervous edge therefore gets deliveredRate=0, so blobSpawnRateHz is 0 and nervous veins never emit flow blobs — the function is a permanent stub, not a computation.

findings.title: footgun: resolveDemandWidth's doc comment says demand edges 'Consistently uses the same structural logic as supply edges' via sourceRadius*drawFraction pulsed width.
findings.detail: resolveDemandWidth (and the resolvePulsedWidth it wraps) is dead — no production or test caller. Demand (resource-demand) edges actually get their width from resolveThrottleWidth in veinsDisplayBuilder.ts, which ignores sourceRadius and drawFraction entirely, so the documented 'consistent' width model is not the one in effect.

findings.title: footgun: getImageUrl wraps its body in a try/catch, suggesting all failures are converted to a rejected promise there.
findings.detail: The try/catch only guards the synchronous resolveDisplayImageSpec + buildDisplayCacheKey. The actual render runs later inside Promise.resolve().then(...) via resolveCached; render-time throws never reach this catch. They still reject the returned promise (through resolveCached's error handler at line 86), so the catch at line 62 is effectively dead for render failures and only ever fires for spec/key errors.

findings.title: footgun: A module-level `const avatarRegistry = new AvatarAppearanceRegistry()` reads like an incidental helper, and DisplayImageExportService separately syncs `this.scene.avatarRegistry` at render time.
findings.detail: This is a process-wide singleton distinct from the scene registry. The request's appearance is resolved from THIS registry (line 52), while the render re-derives from the scene registry; they only agree because resolve() is a pure PRNG of (epochSeed, subjectSeed). The singleton's cache is never cleared and grows unbounded across every avatar built for the life of the tab.

findings.title: footgun: drawGlyphs looks like it always draws a real glyph texture; `textureKey ?? ""` reads as a harmless default.
findings.detail: When scene.textureManager is undefined, getGlyphTexture returns undefined and the key becomes the empty string; readPhaserTextureSource then does scene.textures.get(""), which in Phaser returns the __MISSING placeholder texture rather than throwing, so a missing texture manager silently paints Phaser's checkerboard instead of erroring or the intended glyph.

findings.title: footgun: const LINEAR_FILTER = "LINEAR" as unknown as Phaser.Textures.FilterMode; named LINEAR_FILTER and passed to setFilter, implying the strip gets LINEAR (smooth) filtering like every sibling texture.
findings.detail: The runtime value is the string "LINEAR", not the enum member (which is the number 0). WebGLRenderer.setTextureFilter branches on `filter === 0 ? gl.LINEAR : gl.NEAREST`; the string fails strict-equals, so the texture is actually filtered NEAREST. The name asserts the opposite of the runtime effect.

findings.title: footgun: uniform vec2 uResolution and uniform float uCameraZoom are declared, populated every frame by applyBiologicalFogUniforms, and uResolution is even specially re-pushed in the resize handler, implying the fog reacts to viewport resolution and zoom.
findings.detail: main() never reads uResolution or uCameraZoom (the shader anchors fog purely via uCameraScroll + fragCoord, with zoom baked into the game-object size). The GLSL compiler strips both unused uniforms, so all their setUniform calls target uniforms that do not exist in the linked program; the resize handler's uResolution writes are no-ops.

findings.title: footgun: Parameters _textureManager and _scene are accepted (underscore-prefixed) as if resolution needs the Phaser scene/texture manager.
findings.detail: Both are entirely unused inside the function body; presentation is built purely from the registry appearance and canvas. The signature advertises a scene/texture dependency the code does not have.

findings.title: footgun: config.maxSubSteps (schema-capped at 16) reads as the ceiling on physics substeps per tick.
findings.detail: It is combined via Math.max(configMax, min(requiredSteps,48)) then subSteps=min(requiredSteps,effectiveLimit), which algebraically reduces to subSteps=min(requiredSteps,48) for every input. maxSubSteps never changes the substep count; the real (and only) cap is the hardcoded ABSOLUTE_MAX_SUBSTEPS=48.

findings.title: footgun: ImpulseConfig exposes a user-facing subSteps slider described 'Physics sub-steps per frame' (impulseConfig schema, default 1), implying it controls the tick substep count.
findings.detail: tick() derives subSteps purely from dt (requiredSteps) and the 48-cap; config.subSteps is never read here or anywhere in src, so the slider has no effect on the simulation.

findings.title: footgun: computeObstacleAvoidance takes a general 'neighbors' list and is fed the full spatial query buffer, reading as if it avoids all nearby bodies.
findings.detail: 'if (!neighbor.isStatic) continue;' skips every dynamic body, so only STATIC bodies are ever treated as obstacles; dynamic bodies are never avoided by this path (they rely on separation instead).

findings.title: footgun: queryRadius is documented as returning 'all bodies that *might* collide with the given circle (x, y, radius)'.
findings.detail: It queries a square (half-extent=radius, not a circle) and its containment test only checks each neighbor's CENTER against that box, ignoring the neighbor's own radius, so a large body straddling the query circle from just outside can be missed; it is not collision-complete.

findings.title: footgun: applySeek is exported as part of the steering API, implying it is a live force applied during ticks.
findings.detail: applySeek has zero callers anywhere in src (only computeSeek is used); it is dead exported code.

findings.title: footgun: applySeparation is exported alongside computeSeparation and takes a Quadtree, implying it is the live separation entry point.
findings.detail: applySeparation has zero callers in src; the live path is computeSeparation via ImpulseSteeringForces, and this quadtree-based wrapper is dead code.

findings.title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN plus the broken-reference machinery reads as a general 'detect references to missing blueprints' check.
findings.detail: The pattern /\bentity_[a-z0-9]+\b/i only recognizes ids of the shape entity_<alnum>. Real blueprint/draftOption ids in src/data are nanoid-style (e.g. 0HNjKctJ5pN7Zwr6gV2ay) or human slugs (e.g. Accountant, 30_seconds_in) — 0 of 265 distinct ids are entity_-prefixed — so a missing reference to a real id never becomes a BrokenReference; broken detection fires only for the synthetic entity_ ids used in tests.

findings.title: footgun: ENTITY_ID_PATTERN.test(value) reads as 'this string IS an entity id', so the recorded missingId is the referenced id.
findings.detail: test() is a substring match anchored only by \b word boundaries, not ^...$, so any free-text string that merely contains an entity_ token (e.g. 'spawn entity_foo now') matches, and broken.push records missingId: value = the entire string, not the matched id. The later filter existingIds.has(b.missingId) then compares that whole sentence against the id set.

findings.title: footgun: existingIds.has(value) paired with a case-insensitive ENTITY_ID_PATTERN suggests id resolution is case-tolerant.
findings.detail: existingIds is a Set with exact case-sensitive lookup, while ENTITY_ID_PATTERN carries the i flag. A reference written as entity_A when the blueprint key is entity_a fails existingIds.has (miss), then matches the pattern, and is reported as a broken reference even though a case-variant of the target exists.

findings.title: footgun: applyStatePatch on a handler whose class comment and payload name (PATCH_BLUEPRINT, 'patches live entities') imply patching updates component values on existing entities.
findings.detail: For the 'state' component it ADDS only keys the live entity does not already have (line 19: `if (state[key] !== undefined) continue`); a patched value for an EXISTING state key is silently dropped on live entities even though the blueprint definition itself is updated. The test asserts hp stays 10 after a patch to 1 (PatchBlueprintHandler.test.ts:127).

findings.title: footgun: The `total <= 0` guard logs `Transfer failed: target '<id>' at capacity.`, presenting a zero total as a target-capacity condition.
findings.detail: `total` is the sum of `result.clampedPayload`, which calculateTransaction clamps to BOTH target capacity AND source availability (transferLogic.ts clampToAvailable). A total of 0 also occurs when the source has nothing to send, so the 'at capacity' message misattributes a source-empty (or all-non-positive) transfer to the target being full.

findings.title: footgun: clampPayloadToCapacity is named as if it constrains a transfer payload to the target's remaining capacity.
findings.detail: Only positive, finite amounts are clamped; a non-finite or non-positive amount is copied into the output UNCHANGED (lines 53-55), so a negative or NaN transfer amount bypasses capacity clamping entirely and flows downstream.

findings.title: footgun: The `prefix` parameter (default "spawn", e.g. "pending") looks like it namespaces the id counter per prefix.
findings.detail: The serial is shared across all prefixes via the single sys_world.state.spawnSerial counter; the prefix is only a cosmetic label. Two different prefixes never produce the same numeric serial, but the counter does not restart per prefix (documented in the doc comment, contradicting the per-namespace impression the parameter gives).

findings.title: footgun: The comment 'Mutate in-place so concurrent systems in the same tick see the update' plus the enqueued UPDATE_TRAITS_BATCH command frame this as merely enqueuing a state change, and Snapshot.getEntities() is typed ReadonlyArray<Readonly<RuntimeEntity>>.
findings.detail: executeAddTraitAction/executeRemoveTraitAction cast the readonly snapshot entity to a mutable type and directly push/splice context.self.traits (and even assign self.traits=[] when absent), mutating the live entity object during the read-only behavior phase. The Readonly typing is compile-time only; the entity is aliased into the snapshot, so behavior emits a side effect before its command is applied, unlike every other executor which only enqueues.

findings.title: footgun: The name resolveContention and the ContentionRule framing suggest it only reorders transfer requests that compete for the same target resource.
findings.detail: It returns [...otherCommands, ...sortedTransfers], globally hoisting EVERY non-transfer command (KILL, SPAWN, MUTATE-derived, etc.) ahead of ALL transfer commands whenever the batch contains at least one transfer (see caller runtimeCollectCommands.ts line 20). Relative order between a non-transfer command and a transfer that preceded it in emission order is silently inverted.

findings.title: footgun: getAutomationComponent's comment says 'We trust the data is valid because it was validated on Spawn/Input' and returns the raw object typed as AutomationComponent, implying schema invariants (AutomationComponentSchema enforces intervalMs>=1) hold.
findings.detail: It only checks typeof === 'object' and casts via `as any`; no Zod parse runs. Any code path that writes an automation component with intervalMs of 0 (or a non-integer/negative repeats) is accepted, and resolveNextTiming then computes nextRemaining % 0 = NaN before falling back to intervalMs (0).

findings.title: footgun: applyOperator implements '/' as a normal division operator.
findings.detail: Division by zero returns 0 rather than Infinity/NaN, so an expression like `x / y` silently yields 0 when y resolves to 0 instead of surfacing the degenerate case; downstream mutations treat that 0 as a real computed value.

findings.title: footgun: step() reads as a manual single-frame advance (a public sibling of start/stop that pushes the sim forward one step).
findings.detail: It invokes the callback with dt=0. The wired runtime callback (ui/runtime/state/runtimeFactory) forwards that to runtime.tick(0), and advanceRuntimeCoreTick treats dt<=0 as a no-op (normalizeDt(0)=0 -> returns null), so Ticker.step() advances nothing. The real single-step is RuntimeCore.stepOncePreservingPause(), which passes LOGIC_STEP_MS.

findings.title: footgun: The docstring says "Resets ECS + physics state so game.init can re-spawn a fresh world", implying a full clean-slate reset.
findings.detail: It resets tick to 0 but never touches state.status. A runtime that went "fatal" stays fatal across reset(): RuntimeCore.reset() then calls pause(), which is guarded by status !== "fatal" and so no-ops. Only destroy() clears fatal (to "idle"). Reset does not recover a wedged runtime.

findings.title: footgun: advanceRuntimeCoreTick's parameter type RuntimeCoreTickState declares entityStore/systemPhaseBuffers/systemsRegistry as plain `object`, suggesting the type constrains what is passed.
findings.detail: Those fields are immediately cast to `never` before use (core.entityStore as never, etc.), so the declared `object` type provides no checking; the real contract is whatever tickRuntimeCore requires, enforced nowhere at this boundary.

findings.title: footgun: SaveGameState.timeScale:number is a required field, implying the runtime's time scale is captured and restored across a save/load cycle.
findings.detail: The value is never derived from the live runtime and never read on load. serialize() writes a hardcoded 1 (RuntimeSerializer.ts:40) regardless of the actual RuntimeAccessors timeScale, and hydrateRuntime() never restores it. The field is inert on both ends.

findings.title: footgun: SaveGameState.systems.automation:AutomationSnapshot advertises that automation-system state is part of the persisted save and round-trips.
findings.detail: serialize() writes runtime.getAutomationSnapshot() (RuntimeSerializer.ts:44) but the sole load path hydrateRuntime() never calls setAutomationSnapshot, so the snapshot is silently discarded on every load and automation state does not round-trip.

findings.title: footgun: SerializedPhysicsBody.velocity and the code path body.position.x - body.prevPosition.x read as a physical velocity in units per second.
findings.detail: It is a per-tick position delta (Verlet integration), not a units/second velocity; syncPhysicsBody consumes it by reconstructing prevPosition = position - velocity, and it is intentionally never assigned to the body's separate optional velocity field (which the integrator treats as a one-shot units/second seed). Treating this delta as a real velocity elsewhere would be scaled by the tick rate.

findings.title: footgun: 'cat' claims to 'Display file contents' for any file and the fs layer treats .cvs as a supported semantic file stored as text.
findings.detail: vfs.readFile returns ModuleCartridge|null and discards any string value (FileSystem.base.ts:57 requires typeof!=='string', line 66 returns null for disk text), so `cat <file>.cvs` always reports 'not found' even when the .cvs file exists in the VFS. cat can never show a .cvs (text) file.

findings.title: footgun: 'rm' confirms existence with `const exists = await vfs.readFile(filename)` before deleting, implying it works for any file.
findings.detail: vfs.readFile returns null for text (.cvs) files (FileSystem.base.ts:66), so `rm <file>.cvs` returns 'File not found' and refuses to delete a .cvs file that actually exists in the VFS.

findings.title: footgun: Success message 'Successfully saved to source' and description 'Dump a VFS file to disk' present save as a generally-available persistence action.
findings.detail: vfs.saveToDisk POSTs to the /__editor/save dev middleware and reads via getDiskWritePath; that endpoint only exists under the Vite dev editor plugin. In a production build the fetch hits a non-existent route and save throws / fails; the operation is dev-only, not a real 'save to source'.

findings.title: footgun: handleMakeFile builds a `.cvs` template as the string '# Cave script\n' (line 63) and writes it, and the value is cast `template as ModuleCartridge`.
findings.detail: vfs.writeFile is typed for ModuleCartridge objects; the .cvs string is persisted, but because readFile never returns strings, the just-created .cvs file is subsequently invisible to cat/rm and is dropped by fs-save. The `as ModuleCartridge` cast hides that a string is being stored under an object-typed API.

findings.title: footgun: smartPathUtils imports getFileSuggestions from ./fileUtils (line 2) and getMultipartSuggestions appears to delegate depth-0 completion to it.
findings.detail: A local function getFileSuggestions(token, context) is declared at line 110 and shadows the import; the fileUtils import is unused, and the local one takes (string, context) whereas the imported one takes (string[]). The imported symbol is dead and the two same-named functions have incompatible signatures.

findings.title: footgun: projectRoots() derives project roots by scanning fileCache for manifest paths.
findings.detail: fileCache is populated by refreshFileCache which strips /.cave-dir directory markers but keeps 'manifest.json' entries; however fileCache is only asynchronously refreshed and is clobbered with raw, unfiltered keys by `ls` (lsCommand.ts:14), so project-load/create autocomplete silently reflects a stale or marker-polluted view depending on prior commands.

findings.title: footgun: scan(glob) with a parameter named `glob` implies standard glob semantics where `*` matches within a single path segment and does not cross `/`.
findings.detail: The glob is compiled to an anchored, case-insensitive regex where `*` becomes `.*`, which crosses `/` boundaries. So scan("src/*.json") also matches deeply-nested keys like src/a/b.json, and matching is case-insensitive. Same behavior in the batch path (indexedDbBatch.ts scan, line 79).

findings.title: footgun: Doc comment says "Compare two semantic version strings (e.g. \"1.0.0\" vs \"1.0.1\")", implying real semver comparison.
findings.detail: It only parses dot-separated numeric components with `Number(p) || 0`. Pre-release/build suffixes are not handled: "1.0.0-beta" parses its third component as Number("0-beta")=NaN→0, so "1.0.0-beta" compares equal to "1.0.0"; any non-numeric component silently degrades to 0, and "1.2" vs "1.2.0" are treated as equal (not newer). Drives hydration overwrite decisions (bootstrapHydration.ts:43) and bootstrap manifest selection.

findings.title: footgun: assertValidBootstrapSnapshot is named as if it validates that the data is a valid bootstrap snapshot (i.e. a map of file paths to cartridges).
findings.detail: It only asserts the value is a non-null, non-array plain object that is JSON-serializable. It does not validate keys as paths or values as ModuleCartridge shape, so arbitrary object payloads pass and are later written verbatim into the store by importAll.

findings.title: footgun: `assertValidProjectModules` — the name promises it asserts every listed module is valid and rejects otherwise.
findings.detail: A non-semantic module that fails `ModuleCartridgeSchema` makes `parseProjectModuleFile` return null (projectModuleParsing.ts:25), which the try/catch does not catch; line 95 `if (module)` then silently skips it, so an invalid module is dropped from the returned map without any error. It only throws for a missing file (line 88) or a thrown ZodError.

findings.title: footgun: `for (const [path, mod] of pending.entries())` then `writeModule(path, ...)` — the variable named `path` reads like a resolved absolute file path.
findings.detail: `pending` is keyed by `nextFile`, a project-relative filename (set at line 51), and `writeModule`'s parameter is `filename`. The value is a relative name, not a path; `writeModule` itself resolves it via resolveProjectFile. The name contradicts what it holds.

findings.title: footgun: `stageProjectVersion(manifestPath, currentManifestVersion, changeKind)` reads like a pure function of its arguments.
findings.detail: It reads and mutates the module-level `stagedVersions` Map (process-global singleton). The `currentManifestVersion` argument is ignored on every call after the first for a given path — subsequent bumps are computed from the cached `baseVersion`, not the passed-in version, so passing an updated current version has no effect once a bump is staged.

findings.title: InstantTransferHandler reimplements creditResources instead of reusing the shared one
findings.detail: creditResources and ensureStateRecord here duplicate the semantics of transferResources.ts creditResources (lines 93-125), which the file already imports debitResources from. The two copies have already drifted (error strings 'Transfer failed:' vs 'Credit skipped:'), so a future fix to credit rules must be made in two places or the balancing path will diverge from the runtime path.

findings.title: Self-transfer bypasses the allowDeposit lock
findings.detail: findBlockedDeposit is only consulted when source.id !== target.id, so a transfer whose source and target are the same entity can credit a resource marked allowDeposit:false. If any code issues self-targeted transfers, deposit locks are silently ineffective for them.

findings.title: Scanner iterates behavior-rule actions as untyped `any`
findings.detail: action is typed `any`, so action.type/action.value/action.target are unchecked. A schema change to actions (renamed field, non-numeric value shape) would not be caught by the compiler and would silently drop or misclassify behavior levers.

findings.title: initializeWorldState silently no-ops when world blueprint/entity is absent
findings.detail: If the sys_world blueprint lacks components.state, or no sys_world entity exists, the function returns without initializing world state or the worldSeed, so the simulation runs against whatever default state existed with no signal that world configuration was skipped.

findings.title: Assignment one-off installs a GC rule whose trigger it never fires
findings.detail: For a one-off assignment without a cycle ability, the pushed sys_cycle_gc rule is gated on is_depleted==1, but the assignment path only seeds is_depleted to 0 and nothing sets it to 1 (only the cycle reset rule in cycleCompiler.rules.ts flips it). The entity is therefore never garbage-collected on depletion unless a cycle ability is also present, so a one-off-only assignment silently leaks.

findings.title: Conditional-activation config silently dropped when a gate fails to compile
findings.detail: compileConditionalActivationConfig does `if (!onGate || !offGate) return;` with no warning, so if the structured conditions fail to produce both gates the entire config (its active-state key and both on/off rules) is emitted as nothing. Any ability targeting that conditional-activation slot then references an active-state flag that is never toggled, and the misconfiguration produces no diagnostic.

findings.title: appendRuleConditions drops a malformed gate, leaving the rule ungated
findings.detail: A single unparseable condition string is skipped while its sibling gates and the rule's actions are kept, so a rule that was meant to be gated compiles to one that fires unconditionally (fail-open). The only signal is a console.warn; the compiled blueprint is silently more permissive than authored.

findings.title: toRefPath returns undefined for 5 of 9 condition kinds with no compile-time guard
findings.detail: Latent defect: if a future ref-based condition kind is added to the union and to `toCompiledExpression` (calling `toRefPath`) but the `toRefPath` switch is not extended, it emits `{ var: undefined }` with no type error and no runtime throw, producing a compiled rule that references an undefined var. The missing exhaustiveness check makes this failure invisible at build time.

findings.title: scalableCompiler seeds initial state value only when no per-body scaling is configured
findings.detail: `setInitialValue` (which writes `components.state[key].value|max`) runs only in the no-scaling branch; when perBody/multPerBody scaling is present the initial static field is left untouched and the value is expected to be produced by passiveEffects at runtime. Callers that do not independently declare the target state key (unlike storageCompiler, which pre-creates it) would get a target whose static initial value/max is never seeded, relying entirely on passive-effect evaluation order.

findings.title: Array-valued config sections are overwritten, not accumulated, across semantic files
findings.detail: When multiple .cave files each contribute array config (conditions, guidances, tutorials, knowledge), deepMergeObjects replaces the array wholesale, so all but the last file's entries are silently lost even though multi-file merge is the linker's purpose.

findings.title: Explicit bare blueprint ids bypass namespacing and silently override across files
findings.detail: namespaceBlueprints keeps an explicit non-namespaced id as-is, and mergeRegistry only fires a debug callback on collision before overwriting; two files defining the same explicit id produce a silent last-wins override with no error and no user-visible warning.

findings.title: normalizeBpInput discards sibling blueprints when a top-level id and a blueprints wrapper coexist
findings.detail: If a .bp file has both a top-level `id` and a `blueprints` map, only the entry matching `raw.id` (or the first entry) is kept and re-keyed; any other blueprints in the wrapper are dropped without error, so authored blueprints can vanish from the cartridge.

findings.title: validatePayload never checks draftPool ids, so payloads referencing pools are flagged as broken refs
findings.detail: existingIds is built only from blueprint headers and draftOptions; a fully-qualified reference to a valid draftPool id is not in the set and is reported as a broken reference, failing an otherwise-valid save.

findings.title: CompilerService leaves the internal _editor block on compiled blueprints stored in the cartridge
findings.detail: compile() returns the draft with _editor intact (it only early-returns when _editor is absent), so RuntimeCartridge.blueprints carry authoring-only _editor data that BlueprintV2 does not declare; downstream consumers see undeclared extra state and serialization has to special-case stripping it.

findings.title: Compiler ignores operator precedence; mixed arithmetic/boolean folds strictly left-to-right
findings.detail: The token loop applies every op/keyword in source order with no precedence, so `1 + 2 * 3` compiles to *(+(1,2),3)=9 not 7, and `a AND b OR c` compiles to or(and(a,b),c) regardless of intended grouping. Any rule authored assuming standard precedence silently evaluates to the wrong number/boolean.

findings.title: Tier-2 isolation is enforced on QUERY/SLOT but not on by-id entity access
findings.detail: createLogicDataFacade resolves any unknown top-level var name as an entity id via snapshot.getEntity in ALL modes. json-logic's `var` walks the first path segment, so tier2_entity logic — explicitly blocked from QUERY/QUERY_COUNT (ops.ts:19,33) — can still read arbitrary entities and their fields with `{var:"<entityId>.<field>"}`, defeating the intended tier-2 sandbox.

findings.title: Operator right-hand operand cannot be NOT or a sub-expression
findings.detail: For an `op` token the RHS is read with tokenToAtom(requireToken(index)) rather than consumeAtom(), so `x == NOT y` throws LogicCompileError('Unexpected token keyword') even though NOT is accepted as an AND/OR operand and at expression start. The grammar is asymmetric and rejects otherwise-reasonable comparisons against a negated value.

findings.title: Shared EMPTY_SELF singleton used as default self target
findings.detail: A single module-level EMPTY_SELF = {} is reused as the Proxy target for every evaluation whose context.self is nullish. The facade is read-only today so this is benign, but any future write through the self facade (or a json-logic op mutating `this`) would leak state across unrelated evaluations. It also has no id, so assignmentMap lookups collapse to assignmentMap[''].

findings.title: Stale node-overlay bounds retained when a pretty transfer glyph shrinks out of view
findings.detail: createNodeOverlayDisplayBoundsFromRadius returns null when the resolved radius is <= 0 (radius can collapse as payload/scale drops), and the `if (bounds)` guard then leaves tickCtx.scratch.nodeOverlayDisplayBounds pointing at the previous frame's bounds instead of clearing it. Overlays/hit-testing that key off these bounds keep targeting a location the glyph no longer occupies. TransformModule (line 26) and TransferModule (line 65) both null/replace bounds unconditionally, so this module is the inconsistent one.

findings.title: Simplex permutation cache grows unbounded across many seeds
findings.detail: getPerm memoizes a 512-byte Uint8Array per distinct seed in a module-level Map that is never cleared or size-capped. compileVeinGuidePath calls createSimplex2D(edge.seed) and edge seeds vary per edge/regeneration, so over a long session with many distinct vein seeds the cache accumulates entries for the lifetime of the module, a slow memory leak.

findings.title: Unbounded wave-phase accumulation for nervous veins
findings.detail: advanceWavePhase decrements state.wavePhaseRad every frame with no modulo/wrap. Over a long-running scene the magnitude grows without bound; once it is large the value fed into Math.sin (veinsRopePath.ts:88-93) loses floating-point precision, so the animated waviness of long-lived nervous veins can visibly quantize or jitter. Also forces a full-path recompute every frame (veinsEdgeTick.ts:63-66) because fullPathResolvedForPhaseRad never re-matches.

findings.title: Spawn loop relies on spawnPulse always pushing to avoid a hang
findings.detail: Inside `while (state.spawnCarry >= 1)`, spawnCarry is only decremented after a successful spawn; the `const pulse = state.pulses.at(-1); if (!pulse) continue;` path loops back without decrementing spawnCarry or advancing the ordinal. It is safe only because spawnPulse unconditionally pushes, so .at(-1) is never undefined. If spawnPulse ever early-returns (e.g. pool exhaustion added later), this becomes an infinite loop that freezes the frame.

findings.title: Producer-resource light picked by a fragile duck-typing score
findings.detail: readProducerResource chooses the light color by scoring each state entry on ad-hoc shape heuristics (allowWithdraw/allowDeposit/visible/max presence) rather than an explicit resource marker. Ties resolve to the first-seen key via Object.entries order, and any change to state-entry shape silently reassigns which resource color a node shows, with no error. Latent correctness/coupling risk in the vein/producer visuals.

findings.title: Distress non-physics path makes root/overlay anchor visible with no inverse on recovery
findings.detail: When distress becomes active the tick calls scratch.root.setVisible(true), overlayAnchor.setPosition(target.x,target.y) and overlayAnchor.setVisible(true). On recovery (ratio >= DISTRESS_THRESHOLD) or loss of body/target it calls hideHalos(), which only kills tweens and hides the three halo images (distressHaloHelpers.hideDistressHalos); it never restores overlayAnchor visibility/position or the root visibility. The entity's overlay anchor is left visible and repositioned, and root is left force-shown, leaking distress state into later frames.

findings.title: Progress-bar slot count is a magic 4 duplicating RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS length
findings.detail: createProgressBarSlots hardcodes Array.from({ length: 4 }), while tickProgressBars iterates RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS (currently 4 entries) and indexes input.slots[index]. The invariant that these two counts match is unenforced: adding a 5th position to the constant makes slots[4] undefined, so hideProgressBarSlot(undefined) / tickActiveProgressBarSlot with an undefined slot throws at runtime.

findings.title: Glyph pulse delay lookup can index past delayMsByPosition and propagate NaN
findings.detail: readPulseValue computes ctx.timeMs - glyph.pulse.delayMsByPosition[placement.position]. GlyphPlacement.position is typed 0..8 but GlyphPulseConfig.delayMsByPosition is an unbounded number[] with no length guarantee. If a cartridge supplies a placement whose position exceeds the delay array length, the lookup is undefined, timeMs - undefined is NaN, and getDemandPulse(entityId, NaN) returns NaN (clampPulse(NaN,0,1) === NaN). That NaN survives clamp01 in resolveGlyphPlacementRenderModel and flows into the glyph transform (position/scale/rotation), silently corrupting rendering with no error.

findings.title: AvatarGlyphModule restores scratch.mainImage AFTER destroying the wrapped glyph module
findings.detail: destroy() calls runtime.destroy(...) (glyphModuleRuntime.destroyGlyphImages sets scratch.mainImage = null and releases the glyph images) and then unconditionally reassigns dCtx.scratch.mainImage = preservedMain, the silhouette captured at create time. If the AvatarModule that owned that silhouette has already been destroyed (which nulls mainImage and releases the silhouette to the pool), this writes a released/stale image reference back into scratch.mainImage, defeating the null-out and creating a dangling pooled-object reference dependent on module destroy order.

findings.title: star6 core/fill glyph is not a symmetric 6-point star
findings.detail: The 'star6' case builds two triangles via starPoints(3, outer) (inner radius passed equal to the outer radius, so the points are not a true star) and mirrors the second with `128 - point.y + 10` — an asymmetric +10px vertical offset. The rendered star6 is lopsided and does not match the geometry of the stroke-path drawStar6, producing an off-center/asymmetric glyph texture.

findings.title: Dead draw-function modules diverge from the live rendering path
findings.detail: glyphShapeDrawFns.ts has no importers, and glyphShapeDrawFnsRings.ts contributes only its size constant. These modules define an entire alternate set of shape geometries (e.g. drawStar6 as a Star of David, T=6/10 stroke widths) that no longer render anything. They present as the shape source of truth but are unmaintained; edits here have no effect and they mislead anyone modifying glyph appearance.

findings.title: Preset epoch check keyed on object reference identity
findings.detail: syncEpoch compares `presetsRaw === this.lastPresetsRaw` by reference. A caller that rebuilds an equal-but-new preset object each frame forces a full parsePresets + cache.clear + ordinal reset every call (re-validating every preset and discarding all procedural allocations), while a caller that mutates the same object in place is never picked up. Correctness and cost both hinge on an unstated referential-stability contract.

findings.title: Procedural glyph capacity throws instead of degrading
findings.detail: findNextAvailableOrdinal throws once nextOrdinal reaches MAX_GLYPH_CAPACITY (4^9) with no reserved-signature slots left. Because get() -> allocateProcedural is on the render/resolve path, an exhausted registry turns a request for an unknown display_key into a thrown error that can break the frame rather than falling back to a placeholder glyph.

findings.title: exhaustionLogged flag is a dead store; capacity-exhaustion warning spams every call
findings.detail: The `if (!this.exhaustionLogged)` block only sets the flag and contains no logging; the console.warn sits AFTER the block and fires unconditionally on every get() once variants are exhausted, flooding the console per-entity per-key instead of once. The guarded flag is never read to suppress anything.

findings.title: Tick context shallow-clones the entity every frame when attention light is suppressed
findings.detail: resolveTickEntity returns `{...entity, __attentionLightSuppressed:true}` — a fresh object identity each tick for every non-focused entity during tutorial/announcement focus. Any downstream display module keyed on entity reference identity sees a new object every frame (breaking identity caches), plus a per-entity per-frame allocation.

findings.title: Empty-string entity id collides all id-less entities into one structural record
findings.detail: syncFullRebuild uses `entity.id ?? ''` as the map key; two or more entities lacking an id all map to key '' , so they overwrite each other in the records map and only one gets a visual instance. The same '' also becomes the DisplaySpec.entityId downstream.

findings.title: Structural incremental sync ignores mutationRevision when a full-rebuild trigger also changed
findings.detail: The `else if (syncState.mutationRevision !== mutationRevision)` only runs when fullRebuild is false. On the same tick that a full rebuild fires, syncState.mutationRevision is overwritten by Object.assign without the changed-entity pass running; this is benign only if a full rebuild always supersedes per-entity mutations, which is an unstated assumption.

findings.title: getAvatarPart indexes catalogs but callers pass unvalidated appearance indices
findings.detail: generateAvatar*Texture pass appearance.faceShapeIndex/hairShapeIndex/eyeShapeIndex straight into getAvatarPart, which throws on an out-of-range index. Because assertAvatarAppearance (called first) never checks these indices, a corrupted-but-keyed appearance throws inside texture generation rather than being caught at the guard.

findings.title: Unknown/future visual-event kinds silently become smoke puffs
findings.detail: The dispatcher has no default/reject branch: any event whose kind is not one of the four explicitly handled cases falls through to spawnSmokePuff(scene, layers, textureManager, event.x, event.y, event.radius). A newly added event kind (or any variant lacking x/y/radius) would spawn an unintended smoke puff at undefined coordinates instead of being ignored or flagged. Correct today only because kill_smoke_puff happens to want a puff.

findings.title: Nervous veins render permanently static (no flow blobs)
findings.detail: resolveNervousDeliveredRate always returns 0, so in veinFlowProjection every nervous edge's deliveredRate is 0, making blobSpawnRateHz 0 in veinsDisplayBuilder. Nervous veins are drawn but never animate flow, so an entire vein category is silently inert regardless of runtime state.

findings.title: Dead base-width computation in the display builder
findings.detail: widthPx is initialized with resolveBaseWidth(edge.power, config) but is unconditionally overwritten for both edge kinds (resource-demand -> resolveThrottleWidth, nervous -> resolveNervousWidth), and VeinEdgeKind has only those two members. The resolveBaseWidth call (including its console.error path for invalid power) can never affect output, misleading readers about how vein width is derived.

findings.title: Cluster of dead geometry/color exports with live-looking doc comments
findings.detail: resolveDemandWidth, resolvePulsedWidth (reachable only through resolveDemandWidth), groupEdges, and resolveOffsetStep have no production or test references; resolveVeinColor in colorUtils.ts is likewise unused. They carry authoritative-sounding comments describing width/color behavior that is not actually in effect, inviting future callers to wire up superseded logic.

findings.title: Terminal-target resolution is O(n^2) over the edge list
findings.detail: projectVeinEdgeFlow calls resolveTerminalChainTargetId for every resource-demand edge, and each call scans forward through graph.edges (findNextEdgeIndex) per chain hop. On large graphs this is quadratic in edge count each frame. Fine for current small graphs but a latent per-frame cost that scales poorly.

findings.title: Pointer 'update' scene-event listener is never removed on teardown
findings.detail: attachPointerSceneSystems registers scene.events.on('update', update) but destroyPointerSceneSystems only destroys the controller/preview and deletes the WeakMap entry; it never calls scene.events.off('update', update). The closure stays subscribed and keeps live references to the destroyed PointerPreviewSystem and getRuntime. Every other listener in this subsystem (PointerInputController, EntityDragController) is symmetrically unbound, making this the odd one out. If Phaser reuses the scene instance across a shutdown/restart (same events emitter), the stale handler fires preview.update() on a destroyed preview.

findings.title: resolveBodyAvatarExportInputs is dead production code
findings.detail: The exported function has no non-test importer anywhere in src/ (only its own .test.ts references it); the live avatar path uses buildBodyAvatarImageRequest instead. It duplicates the avatar spec/seed/appearance resolution logic, so the two can silently drift, and it carries a maintained test suite for an unreachable code path.

findings.title: Test-only module (imports vitest) lives in the shipped source tree
findings.detail: This file is not named *.test.ts, so a bundler/tsc pass over src/ will follow it and pull `vitest` (a dev-only dependency) into a production build graph. It is imported only by test files today, but its presence as a plain .ts under scenes/ is a latent build-break / dependency-leak if anything in the product graph ever imports it.

findings.title: resolveDragReleaseUpdate accept-path silently loses the origin-owner guard
findings.detail: When the drop target is valid, the returned update is { bodyId, ownerId } with no expectedCurrentOwnerId, whereas the restore path pins expectedCurrentOwnerId:'sys_pointer'. If the pointer's ownership changed between pickup and release (another assignment mutated sys_pointer), the accept branch applies unconditionally with no optimistic-concurrency check, so a stale drop can reassign a body the pointer no longer legitimately holds.

findings.title: Debug snapshot reaches into runtime/scene internals via untyped casts
findings.detail: previousSnapshot and veinsSystem.graph.edges are read through `as any`, so any rename/reshape of those internals silently degrades to `false`/`0` in the debug panel with no compile error. Debug-only, but the snapshot would misreport health without any signal that the reach-in broke.

findings.title: Malformed background config throws inside the render loop (unlike the safeParse'd camera path)
findings.detail: parseBackgroundConfig uses BackgroundConfigSchema.parse (throws), and it is called from BiologicalFogBackground.update -> GameScene.update every frame with no try/catch. A cartridge whose background config violates a constraint (e.g. intensity < 0, or threshold_low >= threshold_high) makes the scene update throw every frame, breaking rendering. The sibling camera bootstrap deliberately uses safeParse+DEFAULT fallback, so this fragility is specific to the fog path.

findings.title: base_color/lift_color pass schema validation as any string but throw at hex parse in the frame loop
findings.detail: BackgroundConfigSchema types base_color/lift_color as z.string() with only a default (no hex validation), so a value like "purple" or "#12g" is accepted by config parsing but then normalizeHexColor throws `Invalid biological fog color` on every frame of BiologicalFogBackground.update, hard-failing the render loop with no fallback.

findings.title: Avatar presentation cache grows unbounded and is never invalidated
findings.detail: The module-global `cache` Map is only ever written (cache.set) and read, never cleared or size-bounded. Each distinct appearanceKey (which changes across registry epochs/seeds) adds a permanent entry holding three canvas data-URL strings, so over a long session with re-rolled seeds the cache leaks memory monotonically.

findings.title: GLSL variable named `smooth` is a reserved word in GLSL ES 1.00
findings.detail: The fragment shader is GLSL ES 1.00 (precision + varying + gl_FragColor) yet declares `vec2 smooth`; `smooth` is a reserved interpolation qualifier in the ES 1.00 spec. Conformant compilers reject it, so on stricter WebGL1 drivers the fog shader fails to compile and the background silently never appears; it works only because permissive drivers (e.g. ANGLE) tolerate the reserved name.

findings.title: CameraController.bindInput adds pointers/handlers with no matching removal in destroy
findings.detail: bindInput() calls scene.input.addPointer(1) unconditionally when fewer than 2 pointers exist, but destroy() only toggles the event handlers off and never releases the added pointer. Repeated create/destroy cycles of the scene accrete extra input pointers on the shared input plugin.

findings.title: clampToBounds replaces the position object instead of mutating in place
findings.detail: Every other code path mutates body.position.x/y in place, but clampToBounds reassigns body.position to a fresh {x,y}. Any code holding a reference to the previous position Vector2 (renderer, cached alias) silently keeps the stale, unclamped object and diverges from the body.

findings.title: Coincident bodies always separate along +X only
findings.detail: When two bodies are within 0.0001 the code does 'dx += 1; distance = 1;' but never adjusts dy, so exactly-stacked bodies are always pushed apart along +X. Perfectly-overlapping clusters fan out on one axis, producing a directional bias rather than isotropic dispersal.

findings.title: Shared mutable zeroVector singleton returned to callers
findings.detail: computeWobbleForce (and the zeroVector singletons in ImpulseSteeringHelpers.ts:7 and ImpulseAnchor.ts:4) return one shared {x:0,y:0} object. Current callers only read it, but any future consumer that mutates a returned force vector in place would corrupt the global zero for all subsequent callers this frame.

findings.title: Broken-reference detection is inert on real ids: missing references never surface
findings.detail: Because unresolved strings are only reported when they match the entity_ pattern, a payload/pool/blueprint that points at a real but non-existent target (nanoid or slug id) yields an empty broken list. Any consumer that trusts index.broken to catch dangling references gets a false all-clear on production module data.

findings.title: filteredBroken filter is dead code and masks the real dedup intent
findings.detail: broken.filter((b) => !existingIds.has(b.missingId)) can never remove an element: in walk.ts a value is pushed to broken only after existingIds.has(value) has already returned false, so every b.missingId is guaranteed absent from existingIds. The filter is a no-op that reads as a meaningful safety net; if the walk logic later changes to push existing ids, this line silently becomes load-bearing without any test exercising the removal.

findings.title: RESOLVE_TRANSFER credits receiver with no capacity (max) clamp
findings.detail: An existing state entry is incremented by `entry.value += amount` with no reference to `entry.max`. Capacity is only enforced at TRANSFER time (calculateTransaction); if the receiver's max shrinks between initiation and resolution, or for a 'returning' transfer whose source capacity was never checked, resolve overflows the entry above its max. Every other write path (UpdateStateHandler/clampNumeric) clamps to max.

findings.title: Dead unreachable MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD guard
findings.detail: `MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD` is 0 and the preceding guard already returns when `total <= 0`, so `total < MIN_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD` (total < 0) can never be true. The guard is dead code that reads as a configurable minimum-transfer floor but enforces nothing; a future edit to the constant would still be defeated by the `<` (should be `<=`) and the earlier guard.

findings.title: deepMerge of sys_world respawn can accumulate stale array/object state
findings.detail: Re-spawning `sys_world` deep-merges the freshly-built entity into the existing one rather than replacing it. Depending on deepMerge's array/object semantics, previously-accumulated sys_world state (e.g. assignment.assignedIds, serial counters) can persist or blend with blueprint defaults, so a 'respawn to reset' of the world entity does not fully reset it.

findings.title: resolveSpawnOverlap only de-overlaps against the first colliding body
findings.detail: The function returns after resolving the first overlap found in world-iteration order; the pushed-out position is not re-checked against other bodies, so a body spawned into a dense cluster can be relocated onto (still overlapping) a different existing body. Placement quality depends on entity iteration order.

findings.title: AutomationSystem has zero test coverage despite emitting KILL/EXECUTE/UPDATE commands with non-trivial timing math
findings.detail: The repeats-decrement, rollover (nextRemaining % intervalMs), negative-remaining, and repeats===0 kill paths are wired into the runtime tick (RuntimeSystemsRegistry/runtimeSystemPhase) but pinned by no test anywhere in the repo, so a regression in interval/repeat/kill behavior ships undetected.

findings.title: resolveNextTiming decrements repeats by exactly one and enqueues a single EXECUTE regardless of how many intervals a large dt spans
findings.detail: When dt exceeds intervalMs (lag spike, large fixed step, or small interval), the automation fires only once and only loses one repeat that tick; scheduled executions are dropped and the repeat countdown runs slower than wall-clock, diverging from the intended cadence.

findings.title: AutomationSystem contributes soon-to-be-killed automations to the snapshot's nextEventMs/nextCommand
findings.detail: updateSnapshot runs before the repeats===0 kill check, so an automation being killed this tick can still set the reported nextCommand/nextEventMs, making the AutomationSnapshot advertise an event that will never execute.

findings.title: Contention grouping/sorting keys off only the first resource key of a transfer payload
findings.detail: getPrimaryResource takes Object.keys(payload.payload)[0]; a multi-resource transfer would be grouped and rule-matched by an arbitrary single resource. Currently benign because executeTransferAction always emits single-resource payloads, but the resolver silently mishandles any future multi-resource transfer.

findings.title: resolveFromEntity walks arbitrary attacker/author-controlled dotted paths with `any` and no depth bound
findings.detail: A path expression descends entity properties via current[segment] with current typed any; a path landing on a function or exotic property is coerced to 0 silently, and there is no allowlist of readable fields, so state reads depend entirely on blueprint author paths being correct with no validation feedback.

findings.title: Entity sort uses locale-dependent localeCompare on the sim path
findings.detail: getSortedEntities orders entities by id via String.prototype.localeCompare, and this ordering feeds every per-tick Snapshot and thus system iteration order. localeCompare is ICU/locale-dependent, so identical inputs can sort differently across environments/locales, breaking deterministic replay and byte-identical re-carve for any id set where locale collation diverges from code-point order. The in-process determinism test cannot catch this because collation is stable within one process.

findings.title: "fatal" status is not latched against the main tick loop and gets silently cleared
findings.detail: flushCommands/stepOncePreservingPause treat status==="fatal" as terminal (early return), but the main tick path does not: neither advanceRuntimeCoreTick nor runRuntimeTick checks fatal (runRuntimeTick only short-circuits on "paused"). If a fatal runtime is ticked with dt>0 and the substep body completes without re-throwing, advancePhase unconditionally sets status back to "running", clearing the fatal state. The terminal-error invariant is inconsistent across entry points.

findings.title: Command with no registered handler is dropped after only a NOOP-defaulted log
findings.detail: When no handler is registered for a command type, process() logs to the "errors" telemetry channel and continues, discarding the command's intended effect. The command-context telemetry defaults to NOOP_ADAPTER (runtimeTelemetryContext), so if no telemetry adapter is wired the drop is completely silent: a mis-typed or unregistered command vanishes with zero observable trace and no state change.

findings.title: Asymmetric optional-chaining on tutorial.attention can throw
findings.detail: isBlockingOverlayActive guards draft/thought/announcement/guidance with `?.active` but reads `world?.tutorial?.attention.pauseGame` with no optional chain on `attention`. If a sys_world ever carries a tutorial component whose `attention` is missing (partial/hand-built state that bypasses the schema default), this throws a TypeError inside the tick's system phase. A validated TutorialComponent always has attention, so this is latent, but the guarding is inconsistent with the sibling checks and unprotected against malformed state.

findings.title: Substep cap silently discards accumulated time
findings.detail: When the loop hits MAX_RUNTIME_SUBSTEPS, runRuntimeTick returns 0 instead of the still-positive remainingTime, throwing away the unspent accumulator. Under sustained slow frames (accumulator persistently above 10 * LOGIC_STEP_MS) the sim silently drops simulated time rather than falling further behind; time is not conserved, which can desync anything comparing wall-clock to sim time. This is a deliberate spiral-of-death guard but the discard is unannounced.

findings.title: Automation snapshot serialized but silently dropped on load
findings.detail: Every save records automation-system state (pending automation timers/commands) via serialize(), but hydrateRuntime never restores it, so loading a save resets all automation to empty. Players/tests lose in-flight automation with no error, and the save format carries dead payload.

findings.title: Malformed cartridge config throws mid-hydrate after the world is already cleared
findings.detail: hydrateRuntime clears the world first (hydrateRuntime.ts:48), then hydrates the raw sys_world entity, which calls SysConfigSchema.parse (throwing, not safeParse). Any config that fails the schema throws inside the entity loop, leaving the runtime with a wiped world and only the entities processed before sys_world - a corrupted partial state with no rollback.

findings.title: restorePhysicsBody failure is mislabeled invalid_target_physics_component
findings.detail: restorePhysicsBody returns false for two distinct causes (entity absent, or physics schema parse failure), but restoreEntry attributes any false to invalid_target_physics_component. Since the entity was just added and the physics schema was already validated at line 48, this branch is a near-unreachable duplicate check whose issue reason would misdescribe the real cause if ever hit, misleading diagnostics.

findings.title: fs-save silently drops every .cvs file
findings.detail: handleFsSave reads each VFS file with `vfs.readFile(file)` then `if (data == null) continue;`. readFile returns null for .cvs (text) files, so .cvs scripts are never written back to disk. fs-load writes .cvs as text (line 77-79) but fs-save cannot round-trip them: cave-script edits made in the VFS are lost on save with no error.

findings.title: ls pollutes and desynchronizes the autocomplete cache with directory markers
findings.detail: vfs.listFiles() returns all keys including '.cave-dir' directory markers (FileSystem.base.listFiles = db.getAllKeys, no filtering). ls overwrites fileCache with these raw files, whereas refreshFileCache deliberately filters markers (fileUtils.ts:33). After `ls`, file autocomplete for cat/rm/save offers '.cave-dir' marker entries until the next refreshFileCache, and ls output itself lists the internal markers to the user.

findings.title: project-duplicate targets a raw folder named after arbitrary project-name text
findings.detail: targetRoot is set to the trimmed new-name string verbatim (`const targetRoot = newName`) and used directly as a path prefix for writeFile(`${targetRoot}/manifest.json`). A name containing spaces, slashes, or '..' becomes part of VFS keys unsanitized, producing malformed or path-traversing keys; unlike other commands here the target is never run through normalize().

findings.title: Shared workspace/linker/gatekeeper singletons created at module load
findings.detail: ModuleLinker, WorkspaceService, RefactorService and Gatekeeper are instantiated once at import time bound to the global vfs. All project commands share this mutable state (moduleCache, activeCartridge). Concurrent or interleaved project-load/close operations race on shared state, and there is no reset path other than closeProject; a failed load can leave activeCartridge/moduleCache inconsistent for later commands.

findings.title: getMultipartSuggestions depth dispatch indexes an array that omits depth 0
findings.detail: depthHandlers has undefined at index 0 and handlers for indices 1-3; `depthHandlers[segments.length]?.(...)` returns [] for any path deeper than 3 segments (index >= 4 is undefined). Combined with the module having no non-test importer, this rich virtual-path completion is dead code whose deepest levels silently no-op.

findings.title: project-save-blueprint version bump can silently no-op
findings.detail: After a successful write, `if (manifestPath)` guards stageProjectVersionInVfs. workspaceService.getManifestPath() returning falsy (no active/loaded project) skips the version bump entirely with a success result, so a saved blueprint can persist without its project version being incremented, breaking the assumption that every save stages a patch.

findings.title: deletePaths and movePaths bypass dirty-file tracking, leaving stale/lost dirty state
findings.detail: deleteFile clears dirtyFiles, but deletePaths (line 31) and movePaths (line 42) do not touch dirtyFiles. Deleting a dirty file via deletePaths leaves its path permanently in dirtyFiles (getDirtyFiles reports a file that no longer exists); moving a dirty file leaves the OLD path marked dirty and the NEW path unmarked, so a subsequent saveToDisk of the new path is not tracked and the phantom old path lingers. getDirtyFiles consumers see an inaccurate change set.

findings.title: moveMany applies all writes before all deletes over a single key snapshot, so overlapping moves can delete a just-written value
findings.detail: allKeys is captured once; writes (moved targets) are flushed first, then every matched source key is deleted. When a move target collides with another move's source (e.g. moving a/b→a while a/b/c also exists, or two moves whose target equals another's source), the delete phase removes a key that the write phase just populated, silently dropping data. The write/delete sets are computed independently with no collision guard.

findings.title: importAll clears the entire store before writing, with no shape validation of entries
findings.detail: importAll opens a readwrite tx, clears the store, then puts every top-level key of the (only structurally-validated) snapshot as a file value. A snapshot that passes assertValidBootstrapSnapshot but contains non-cartridge or non-path entries wipes existing data and repopulates the store with garbage; the pre-clear means a malformed-but-JSON-serializable import destroys the prior VFS contents irrecoverably.

findings.title: Namespace rename matches by prefix, corrupting sibling namespaces
findings.detail: `ns.startsWith(oldNamespace)` and `replaceRefs`/filename `.replace(oldNamespace, ...)` treat the namespace as a bare prefix/substring: renaming `foo` also rewrites `foobar`, `foo2`, and any `foo::`-prefixed ref inside an unrelated `foobarbaz::` string. Unrelated modules get silently moved and their refs mangled.

findings.title: String.replace rewrites only the first occurrence of a namespace
findings.detail: `filename.replace(oldNamespace, newNamespace)` (line 41) and `file.replace(oldNamespace, newNamespace)` (line 65) use the single-match form of replace. If a filename or manifest entry contains the old namespace more than once, only the first is rewritten, leaving a half-renamed path that no longer resolves. `replaceRefs` uses replaceAll and is correct, so refs and filenames diverge.

findings.title: Global staged-version Map leaks and cross-contaminates instances
findings.detail: `stagedVersions` is a module-level Map shared by every WorkspaceService/RefactorService in the process. Entries are only removed by explicit clearStagedProjectVersion, so an abandoned project (or a test that stages but never persists) leaks its entry forever, and two consumers acting on the same manifestPath see each other's pending bump. In tests this makes version-staging order-dependent and stateful across cases.

findings.title: Manifest re-read via readFile can silently reset the manifest to empty
findings.detail: `(await this.vfs.readFile(manifestPath)) ?? { files: [] }` uses FileSystemBase.readFile, which returns null when the stored value is a string / only present on the text path (FileSystem.base.ts:57,66). On that path the fallback `{ files: [] }` is written back, discarding the real name, version, and file list — a full manifest wipe. loadProject uses readProjectManifest (object-or-text aware) but this refactor path does not.

findings.title: Runtime rebuilt from an arbitrary first cache entry
findings.detail: `replaceRuntime` seeds a new Runtime from `Array.from(this.moduleCache.values())[0]` — the first module by Map insertion order, not the linked/compiled cartridge (activeCartridge) and not a designated entry module. Which single module becomes the runtime depends on manifest.files ordering, and the compiled activeCartridge produced by the linker is not what the runtime runs.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: debitResources skips any key whose entry is missing on the source (`if (entry)`), silently dropping that portion of the debit with no log. Benign for the InstantTransferHandler path because clampToAvailable already filters keys with no numeric source value, but the helper itself gives no trace if reused where the payload can name absent keys.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: initializeWorldState returns early on a missing world blueprint state or missing world entity without logging; a misconfigured cartridge produces a silently unseeded/unconfigured world rather than an error. Real gap for diagnosing bad cartridges.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real. `compileConditionText` returns a discriminated `{ok:false,error}` result; on failure the code logs `console.warn` and does not push the gate, so the error return is effectively swallowed. The rule is still emitted without the intended gate, so a typo in an author's condition text silently downgrades a gated rule to an always-firing one rather than failing the compile.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: a blueprint id collision between two loaded files is only surfaced through an optional onCollision callback wired to logger.debug; if the callback is omitted (or debug is a no-op) the earlier blueprint is overwritten with no error and no operator-visible signal.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Benign-ish: an unsupported file listed in the manifest is skipped with only a logger.warn and readFragment returns null; the file is silently excluded from the cartridge rather than failing the link, so a typo in an extension drops content without erroring.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: on a schema failure only the FIRST zod issue's message is put in the thrown LinkerValidationError (issues[0]); all other validation issues for that file are discarded, so an author fixing one error at a time never sees the rest.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: QUERY returns [] when __snapshot is absent OR tag is not a string. A malformed tag (number/undefined) is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty query result, so a typo'd or wrong-typed tag silently evaluates as 'no matching entities' rather than erroring — real: can mask authoring mistakes in rules.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: QUERY_COUNT returns 0 when __snapshot is absent OR tag is not a string, conflating a malformed/wrong-typed tag with a legitimate count of zero; a rule gated on QUERY_COUNT(badTag) > 0 silently never fires. Real for rule correctness, benign for crash-safety.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
