findings.detail: SLOT returns [] when slotName is not a string (and [] for a missing slot), so a mistyped slot reference yields an empty entity list instead of an error. Combined with SUM (which returns 0 for non-arrays), a broken SLOT path silently produces 0 downstream. Real: masks slot-name authoring errors.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: tickInstanceSafe wraps instance.tick in try/catch that only console.errors and swallows the exception. Real risk: a module that throws mid-tick is silently skipped every frame, so a persistently broken display renders nothing (or stale) with only console noise and no surfaced failure; the frame loop keeps running as if healthy.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: validateScratchSlots detects leaked scratch objects (backgroundImage/mainImage/particles/rope/graphics) but only logs them; it neither destroys nor clears them and the anchors are released regardless. Real risk: leaked Phaser objects accumulate undetected apart from console output, a genuine resource leak masked as a mere warning.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: setInstanceInteractionBlocked calls target.disableInteractive?.() via optional chaining and returns its result; if the target lacks input and lacks the method, the call no-ops silently and interaction is neither blocked nor restored. Mostly benign (best-effort on a loosely-typed target) but can leave a non-focused entity interactive during a tutorial focus lock.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: resolveHeartbeatPreset evaluates operator-authored JsonLogic rule conditions via adapter.evaluate with no try/catch here or in heartbeatRules.ts. If the adapter throws on a malformed rule, the exception propagates up through VeinsSystem.update unhandled every frame rather than degrading to the default preset. Real if rule authoring can produce an evaluation error; benign only while all rules are guaranteed well-formed.

findings.title: silent failure: fire-and-forget
findings.detail: spawnGoldRings starts a tween whose onComplete is the only path that returns the acquired pooled ring image (pool.release). The tween handle is discarded and there is no scene-shutdown/cancellation hook, so if the scene or tween manager is torn down before the ~620ms+stagger completes, onComplete never runs and the ring is never released back to runtime_effects.imagePool — a pooled-resource leak. Benign in steady state, real across scene teardown/restart.

findings.title: silent failure: fire-and-forget
findings.detail: spawnSmokePuff schedules emitter.destroy() via scene.time.delayedCall(420, ...) and ignores the returned timer event. If the scene is shut down before 420ms elapses, the delayed call may not fire and the particle emitter added to the EffectsGlobal layer can be left undestroyed. Benign under Phaser's normal scene timer cleanup, potentially real on abrupt teardown.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Mostly benign by design: the loop tries each module source and swallows a throwing source to fall through to the next candidate, returning null only if all fail. Risk: the catch is bare (no reason comment, no logging), so a genuinely malformed asset that throws for every source is indistinguishable from 'display key legitimately absent' — both surface as a silent null and a missing icon, with no diagnostic breadcrumb.

findings.title: silent failure: fire-and-forget
findings.detail: Real leak: the 'update' listener is attached but never detached on destroy (see risks). The subscription outlives the systems it drives, retaining the destroyed preview and runtime accessor; on scene reuse it invokes preview.update() against torn-down state. Not benign under any scene restart/sleep-wake cycle.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Low-impact: drawPlaceholder returns a boolean success flag that the caller discards. When the placeholder variant or its texture is missing, drawPlaceholder returns false and draws nothing; the render then returns a blank data-URL with no error and no fallback. Benign for present assets, but a missing placeholder texture fails invisibly (empty icon) rather than signaling.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Real risk: the try wraps registry resolution, seed resolution, and canvas rendering (buildBodyAvatarPresentation, which throws on a missing 2d context). Any genuine defect there is swallowed and returns null, so the caller silently renders no avatar with zero diagnostics. No pdd-ignore marker is present.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Mostly benign: `store()` swallows localStorage.setItem failures (private-mode/quota) so the debug toggle still works in-memory. But the empty catch has no pdd-ignore comment and also hides unexpected errors; persistence silently stops with no signal.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Benign-by-intent but unmarked: readStored() catches localStorage access errors and defaults to false. Reasonable fallback, but there is no pdd-ignore reason comment distinguishing the deliberate swallow from an accidental one.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: setWorldBounds silently returns (no-op) when width/height are non-finite or below config.minWorldSize, giving the caller no signal. A caller that passes a too-small or NaN size believes bounds were set while the engine keeps its previous/null bounds, leaving the simulation effectively unbounded (clampToBounds becomes a no-op).

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Mostly benign: setTarget returns silently when bodyId is not in the map, so a mistimed setTarget for a not-yet-added or already-removed body is dropped with no error or return value; the seek simply never engages and the failure is untraced.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: REAL: an unresolved string reference that does not match ENTITY_ID_PATTERN hits the bare `return` and is dropped with no incoming entry and no broken entry. Since real blueprint/draftOption ids are not entity_-prefixed, a dangling reference to a missing real id (e.g. a draft payload blueprintId or a pool optionId pointing at a deleted 'Accountant') fails completely untraced — the index looks healthy while the graph is broken.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: when `assignTo` is set but `context.commands` is undefined, the deferred ASSIGN_BODIES_BATCH is silently dropped with no telemetry, so a body spawns unassigned without any error. The sibling call enqueuePendingBodyHabitiUpdate logs an error on the same missing-commands condition, so this omission is an inconsistency, not a deliberate no-op.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Mostly benign but trace-losing: ensureStateEntry returns silently when the entity exists but has no state object, or the target key is absent/non-numeric (lines 12-14, 24-30). The command reports no error (the outer handle only logs on entity-not-found), so an ADJUST_STATE that hits a missing/invalid entry no-ops invisibly, unlike UpdateStateHandler which creates the entry. Diagnostically silent.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Benign-by-design but undiagnosed: when the pending entity referenced by RESOLVE_TRANSFER is not found, the handler returns with NO telemetry (bare `return`), unlike every other not-found path in the partition which logs to 'errors'. A resolve targeting an already-removed/duplicated pending id vanishes without a trace.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real silent drop: applyStatePatch skips (continues past) any incoming state key that already exists on the live entity, discarding the patched value with no log. A caller patching an existing state value on live entities gets no signal that the update was ignored.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Division by zero is swallowed to 0 (right===0 ? 0 : left/right) with no signal. A misconfigured expression dividing by a resolved-zero denominator produces a silent 0 that flows into MUTATE/TRANSFER amounts; looks healthy, wrong value. Real if any authored expression can divide by a state value that reaches 0.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: resolveNextTiming guards a non-finite/non-positive rollover by falling back to automation.intervalMs, but if intervalMs itself is 0 (schema not re-validated here) the fallback is 0, yielding an UPDATE_AUTOMATION with remainingMs 0 that re-fires every tick with no error. Benign only while every writer honors intervalMs>=1; nothing in this system enforces it.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: The action-type switch has no default branch; an unrecognized BehaviorAction.type (e.g. a new/typo'd action) falls through and is silently dropped with no command emitted and no warning. Mostly benign because the TS union constrains authored actions, but any runtime-constructed or schema-drifted action is a no-op that looks like it ran.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real when unwired: an unhandled command type is dropped in process() with only a telemetry.log to the "errors" channel; because the default command-context telemetry is NOOP_ADAPTER (runtimeTelemetryContext), absent an injected adapter the dropped command produces no state effect and no trace. Benign only if a real telemetry adapter is always wired and monitored.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: REAL: data.state.systems.automation is present in every SaveGameData (written by serialize) but hydrateRuntime consumes only tick/entities/physics and never restores the automation snapshot; the automation portion of the save is silently ignored, so automation state is lost on load without any warning.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: MOSTLY BENIGN: resolveRestoredParents silently deletes an entity's parent (delete entity.parent) when a target-spec parent cannot be resolved to an existing entity. This is intended fallback (an unresolvable parent is dropped rather than left dangling), but it happens with no issue recorded, so a carryover entity that loses its parent linkage does so invisibly.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Benign-by-intent but undeclared: refreshFileCache().catch swallows any VFS listFiles rejection with only a comment 'Silent failure for autocomplete cache'. If the VFS is persistently broken, autocomplete silently shows a stale/empty list with no user signal; no pdd-ignore marker.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: inside handleFsLoad's Promise.all, each per-file read does `if (!res.ok) return;` — a failed read of an individual file is skipped silently, yet the command still reports `Loaded ${files.length} file(s)` counting files that were never actually written. Partial loads masquerade as full success.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real: same pattern as fs-load — `if (!res.ok) return;` per file, then reports `Hard-reloaded ${files.length} file(s)`. After destructively wiping the entire VFS (line 20), any file that fails to re-read is silently missing while the success message claims the full count, so data loss is reported as success.

findings.title: silent failure: fire-and-forget
findings.detail: Mostly benign: refreshFileCache() is invoked without await (it returns a promise resolved internally). rm returns success before the autocomplete cache is actually rebuilt; a rejection is swallowed by refreshFileCache's own catch, so the deleted file can linger in autocomplete briefly. Same fire-and-forget pattern in makeCommands.ts:108/130 and bootstrapLoadCommand.ts:18.

findings.title: silent failure: unchecked-exit
findings.detail: Real: handleProjectClose calls `await workspaceService.closeProject()` with no try/catch; if closeProject rejects, the registry's outer catch reports a generic 'Execution failed', but context.runtime?.unload() and ui?.closeWorkspace() (lines 118-119) are then never reached, leaving runtime/UI in a half-open state. Unlike the other project handlers, close has no local error handling.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Partial: handleFsSave returns an error on the first failed /__editor/save (line 124-128) but files already written before the failure remain on disk, and any file whose VFS data is null (all .cvs) is skipped via `continue` (line 117) and excluded from the reported saved count — a half-completed save reported without indicating which files were skipped.

findings.title: silent failure: empty-catch
findings.detail: Real: the try/catch around the disk fetch swallows every error (network failure, CORS, malformed JSON from response.json()) and returns null with no logging or pdd-ignore marker. Callers readFile/readText interpret null identically to "file absent", so a transient fetch/parse failure is indistinguishable from a missing file and can silently yield an empty read or trigger create_empty hydration, masking real I/O errors.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real. `parseProjectModuleFile` returns null when a non-semantic module fails ModuleCartridgeSchema (projectModuleParsing.ts:25); the guard `if (module)` drops it with no throw and no log, so loadProject proceeds with an incomplete moduleCache and activeCartridge as if the invalid module never existed. A malformed module silently disappears from the project instead of failing the load.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Mostly benign but silent. `reloadModules` returns early when no project/root is loaded, doing nothing and returning void — a caller expecting the modules to have been reloaded gets no error and no signal that the reload was skipped.

findings.title: silent failure: ignored-return
findings.detail: Real. In reloadModules, `const mod = await this.vfs.readFile(...)` then `if (mod) this.moduleCache.set(...)`: a filename that reads back as null (missing on disk, or stored as a string so readFile returns null) is skipped silently, leaving the stale prior cache entry in place with no error, so the reload appears to succeed while that module is unchanged.
